name: Velra Black Sesame-Honey Chews
manufacturer: Velra Artisan Foods (Tier 3 boutique, independently owned)
description: Dense, chewy nougat-style blocks made with black sesame paste and synth-honey compound, cut by hand into irregular squares and wrapped in rice paper. Sold in small cloth-tied boxes of eight.
flavor_profile: Nutty, slightly bitter black sesame base with a rounded honey sweetness; dense and satisfying chew that softens slowly; faint toasty finish
cultural_context: Velra is a small-batch brand with a fiercely loyal following. The cloth-tied boxes are frequently reused for small gifts and storage. Velra's founder gives quarterly interviews about refusing acquisition offers, which has become part of the brand mythology.
story_hooks: Velra's synth-honey supplier has been quietly substituting a cheaper compound for three batches — the taste difference is subtle, but Velra's most dedicated customers have noticed and are organizing online.

The cloth wrapping on Velra boxes is sourced from a single weaver collective in the Shelf district — a development project threatens to displace them, and Velra's public support of the collective has made the brand a political flashpoint.
A Tier 5 collector is attempting to acquire every limited seasonal Velra release — her obsession has become strange enough that Velra's founder is genuinely uncomfortable with the attention.
related_entities: Tessera Corponation ChronoMark VR-3 Passive Isotopic Citizen Tagging System
